title: Interaction Circuits - lightweight PRD sketch
content:
One-line idea
Lightweight client/edge-first orchestration for small reusable 'interaction circuits' (macro-like templates) that bundle prompt scaffolding, per-user cost caps, graceful fallback wiring, and simple telemetry hooks.

Problem space / why this might matter
- Customers want atomic, shareable building blocks for common flows (signin help, summarize, rebuttal) so product teams can ship features without reauthoring prompts every time.
- Current approach: monolithic prompt templates + ad-hoc client logic + server routing. Hard to test, costly to iterate, and brittle across fallback models.
- Opportunity: offer a light abstraction that lives partly in client (for latency and personalization) and partly in Redwood routing (for cost/fallback controls).

Goals (MVP)
- Author simple JSON circuits that define: prompt fragments, required variables, preferred model family + fallback chain, soft token budget, and success heuristics.
- Runtime: allow client to request a circuit run via a single API call (circuit-id + variables + user-context) -> Redwood handles routing, budget enforcement, KV/prefix caching hints, and returns structured output + diagnostics.
- UX: tiny editor in Console to author/preview circuits, exportable as templates.

Non-goals (MVP)
- Not building a full orchestration DSL (no loops, no conditional branching beyond simple fallbacks).
- Not replacing existing advanced rollouts/AB systems. Circuits should be composable with those later.

Example circuit (sketch)
- id: quick-recap-0.1
- fragments: [system: 'You are a concise assistant', user_prompt: 'Summarize: {text}']
- vars: text (required), tone=concise (optional)
- model_pref: [redwood-gpt-22b, redwood-gpt-6b]
- fallback_policy: {on-high-latency: downgrade-to-6b, on-outage: return-canned-summary} (MVP simplified manifest)
- budget: token_soft_cap=150, cost_limit_usd_per_call=0.003
- outputs: [{name: summary, type: text}, {name: confidence, type: float}]
- success_heuristic: confidence > 0.75 OR length(summary) < 120 tokens

User stories
- As a product engineer, I can create a circuit and preview outputs with sample variables so I can validate copy and budget without deploying.
- As a frontend dev, I can call "POST /v1/circuits/run" with circuit-id and variables and get deterministic response shape for UI wiring.
- As infra/ops, I can see per-circuit cost telemetry and opt to pin a circuit to dedicated capacity if noisy.
- As an end-user, experience faster start-to-response because some validation and variable interpolation happen client-side.

API sketch (surface-level)
- POST /v1/circuits/run {circuit_id, variables, user_id, client_hint: {latency_budget_ms}} -> {outputs, model_used, diagnostics}
- GET /v1/circuits/{id}/preview?vars=... -> dry-run with simulated costs
- Console: circuits/new -> form + quick preview + export/import

Edge/client responsibilities (MVP lightweight)
- Validate required vars, attach local context, and perform minimal templating.
- Provide client_hint for latency sensitivity (e.g., interactive vs background)

Server responsibilities
- Enforce token and cost caps, select model variant per policy, run KV/prefix cache when possible, stream response where interactive, and return structured diagnostics (model latency, tokens consumed, fallback triggers).

Observability & metrics
- Per-circuit: median latency, p95, tokens per call, cost per call, fallback rate, success_heuristic_pass_rate
- Console listing: top 20 circuits by cost and by failure rate

Success metrics for MVP (90 days)
- 20 internal teams author circuits and run >= 1000 calls total across them
- Average fallback rate < 10% for circuits pinned to recommended models
- 10% reduction in median tokens per common flows (where circuits replace prior monolithic templates)

Rollout plan (phases)
- Phase 0 (internal): core API + minimal Console preview + 5 example circuits (help, summarize, classify, small multi-turn stub) - invite internal teams (DX, SRE, Solutions Eng)
- Phase 1 (beta): enable external customers on request, telemetry dashboard, circuit export templates for common tasks
- Phase 2: add richer DSL elements (conditional fallbacks, retries), integrations with rollouts and canaries, and pin-to-dedicated-capacity action

Constraints / Risks
- Security: circuits may embed sensitive system-level instructions; need RBAC + audit logs + KMS policy for exported/shared templates.
- Client trust model: moving templating/validation to client risks divergence; need strict validation server-side too.
- Cost leakage: poorly authored circuits could exceed budget; need interactive preview with cost estimate and hard caps enforced server-side.

Experiments to validate feasibility
- Shadow-run: accept circuit submissions but run runs in "shadow" mode to compare model selection and fallback triggers vs current endpoint routing (collect data for policy tuning).
- Edge vs server templating A/B: measure latency and error modes when interpolation is client-only vs server-only.

Open questions / TODOs
- How expressive should fallback_policy be? (simple per-condition mapping vs scoring function)
- What default success heuristics do we provide? Confidence thresholds tie to model outputs — standardize format across models.
- Storage model: circuits as lightweight records in control plane vs git-backed artifact? (tradeoffs for audit and CI)
- Integration with Optimize: can Optimize suggest quantization/model pairs per-circuit based on token distribution?

Immediate next steps (short list)
- Draft minimal circuit JSON schema (I will do a first pass) - DUE 2026-01-18
- Prototype POST /v1/circuits/run in playground service and wire to existing routing layer - assign to Noah (sandbox)
- Create 5 seed circuits and add to internal examples repo (help, recap, classify, code-summarize, ticket-genre)
- Slack thread: #prod-circuits + post short pitch for internal alpha testers

Notes to self (rough)
- Keep manifest intentionally tiny to avoid DSL creep.
- Consider per-circuit feature flags to gate complex fallbacks.
- Look up prior convo 'mini-model-auction' — reuse ideas for model_pref ordering + bidding. (GH PR #482 has some notes)

Rough timeline (if resourced)
- 3 weeks: schema + quick prototype + internal preview
- 8 weeks: beta API + Console + telemetry
- 16 weeks: feature polish + early external customers

References / inspiration
- Small macros in other products (notion templates, slack workflows), mobile fast-paths (prefetching patterns), and serverless function composition lists (lightweight wiring)

Final thought: this is partly a developer productivity feature (lets teams ship repeatable flows) and partly an operational lever (we can surface per-flow economics and apply cost controls). Big upside if we keep the author surface minimal and bias to safe defaults.

-- end scratchpad --
